summary: Fourteen days of Nightscout data with high CGM quality (98.7 percent coverage, 5-minute cadence, 3995 valid entries, no invalid or duplicate readings). Overall glucose metrics are reasonable: mean 121.6 mg/dL, time in range 86.0 percent, coefficient of variation 32.6 percent. The dominant pattern is not hyperglycemia but low glucose: time below range is 5.1 percent overall, above 4 percent on 8 of 14 full days and 12.8 percent on 2026-08-18, with level-2 values of 41, 42 and 42 mg/dL. Local-time patterns show two reciprocal windows: an elevated block from 09:00 to 17:00 peaking at 16:00 (mean 162.8 mg/dL, 32.1 percent above range) and two low-biased windows at 18:00 to 19:00 (time below range 7.7 and 15.3 percent) and 23:00 to 03:00 (10.1 to 18.5 percent). No carbohydrate has been entered in the whole period (0 carb entries, 0 g total, COB 0 in every loop snapshot), so all meal coverage is delivered reactively by UAM and SMB after the rise has started. Dynamic ISF is active with a 70 percent adjustment factor and produces effective sensitivity between 27.8 and 124 mg/dL per unit against a flat profile ISF anchor of 56, roughly twice as strong as the profile value at high glucose. Insulin on board reached 4.73 U and 5.935 U, followed by falls such as 234 to 56 mg/dL in 120 minutes and 264 to 96 mg/dL in 120 minutes. The morning window 04:00 to 08:00 is the best controlled part of the day and needs no change.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM data quality is good and supports time-of-day analysis: 3995 valid entries, 0 invalid, 0 duplicates, 98.7 percent coverage, estimated cadence 5.0 minutes, 10 gaps with a largest gap of 65 minutes. The first day 2026-08-07 has only 33 readings and is not representative. Local time is UTC+1 (BST); hourly_glucose_local equals hour_utc plus one and is used for all time-of-day statements. The AAPS profile is complete and authoritative under profile_context (authoritative_source aaps_profile, historical_applicability yes): 7 basal segments totalling 16.2 U per day, 5 carb ratio segments, one flat ISF segment of 56 mg/dL per unit, three target segments and DIA 10 h. All 17 profile inventory items and all 6 AAPS inventory items were reproduced with their current values. Carbohydrate telemetry is entirely empty (carb_entries 0, total_carbs_g 0.0, carb_treatment_entries empty, extended_carb_entries 0), so carb-ratio and absorption inferences are not supportable. Only representative subsets are supplied (40 of 2315 treatments, 24 of 6214 device statuses, 16 curated extremes, 24 therapy response windows). Context changes inside the window: AAPS start 2026-08-09, profile switch 2026-08-13, site changes 2026-08-10, 2026-08-13 and 2026-08-17, sensor changes 2026-08-11 and 2026-08-21, occlusion and pump error on 2026-08-19, GLP-1 1.25 mg on 2026-08-14, 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-20.

It cannot be determined whether total_insulin_u of 275.95 U includes basal delivery, so the basal to bolus split and true total daily dose are unknown. analysis_steps.findings: Hypoglycemia is the leading safety signal. Overall time below range is 5.1 percent, above the commonly used 4 percent limit, while time in range 86.0 percent and coefficient of variation 32.6 percent are acceptable. Eight of fourteen full days exceed 4 percent below range: 2026-08-10 at 6.9, 08-11 at 9.4, 08-12 at 7.6, 08-14 at 8.3, 08-15 at 4.2, 08-16 at 6.3, 08-17 at 4.9 and 08-18 at 12.8 percent. Level-2 lows appear as clusters rather than single points: 2026-08-13 from 17:59 local, 51, 47, 42, 45 mg/dL, and 2026-08-14 from 19:04 local, 48, 41, 41 mg/dL, both in the evening window; plus a single 42 mg/dL on 2026-08-21 at 07:19 local shortly before a sensor change the same day, which may be a sensor artefact. Highs are shorter and cluster around midday and late afternoon: 285 to 293 mg/dL on 08-15 and 08-18. Large fall amplitudes follow highs: 234 to 56 mg/dL in 120 minutes, 264 to 96 mg/dL in 120 minutes, 206 to 53 mg/dL in 180 minutes, 172 to 47 mg/dL in 240 minutes. Peak insulin on board reached 4.73 U and 5.935 U against a profile basal of 16.2 U per day. On 2026-08-19 an occlusion and a pump error were recorded at 14:40 local, which is a delivery-integrity explanation for part of that day and means recorded IOB may not equal delivered insulin.

analysis_steps.findings: By local hour the day splits into three clearly different blocks. The window 04:00 to 08:00 is the best controlled part of the day (means 99.5 to 110.5 mg/dL, time below range 1.3 to 4.8 percent, time above range at most 1.8 percent) on basal 0.6, 0.7 and 0.8 U/h, so there is no dawn defect and the morning basal steps look appropriate. The window 23:00 to 03:00 is low-biased (means 90.6 to 105.7 mg/dL with time below range 10.1, 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent) on a flat 0.6 to 0.7 U/h and a target of 90 mg/dL. The window 09:00 to 17:00 is high-biased, peaking at 16:00 with mean 162.8 mg/dL and 32.1 percent above range, exactly where basal is at its lowest daytime value of 0.5 U/h. That coincidence is not sufficient to call the 16:00 segment a defect, because carbohydrate is never announced and the same afternoons are followed by the evening lows. Overnight the loop is already removing insulin rather than adding it, with zero temp basals on 2026-08-10, 08-16 and 08-17 and negative IOB of -0.481, -0.197 and -0.03 U, which means the overnight lows cannot be corrected by automation and point to either profile basal or an insulin tail from earlier dosing. Targets are a special case: although the declared target segments are 90, 100 and 90 mg/dL, the loop operated with effective target_bg values between 80 and 116 mg/dL, and only five temporary targets exist in the period (135 mg/dL four times, 108 mg/dL once), so temporary targets do not explain that spread. Declared profile targets therefore appear to have weak leverage in this build and any target edit may not reach the loop as expected.

analysis_steps.findings: Carb ratio cannot be assessed at all: there are zero carb entries, zero meal boluses and COB 0 in every loop snapshot, so the five segments 13, 11.1, 13.2, 10.5 and 12.6 g/U have no observable effect and must not be changed. ISF is declared flat at 56 mg/dL per unit, but it is not the operative value because dynamic sensitivity is enabled with a 70 percent adjustment factor: observed effective sensitivity ranges from 124 mg/dL per unit at glucose 70 and 111.9 at glucose 95 down to 42.5 at glucose 135 with high deviation, 37.9 at glucose 262 and 27.8 at glucose 246. At high glucose the loop therefore doses roughly twice as strongly as the declared profile ISF, which is the most plausible mechanical link between the afternoon peaks and the evening and overnight lows. The therapy response windows cannot be used to derive ISF numerically, because the insulin_u field records only the discrete bolus of 0.05 to 2.4 U while SMB and temp basal delivery continues through the window; for example 0.2 U is associated with a 178 mg/dL fall in 120 minutes. DIA of 10 h with free_peak_oref is long and keeps insulin on the books deep into the tail, which is consistent with the observed 4.73 and 5.935 U peaks and the delayed falls. However dynamic ISF strength, DIA length and the build-specific UAM boost terms all predict the same late-hypoglycemia signature, and the supplied data does not separate them, so no DIA or ISF anchor change is justified in this cycle.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are both enabled and are coherent with the regimen: with zero carb entries UAM is the only mechanism providing meal coverage, so disabling it would enlarge the 09:00 to 17:00 elevated block. UAM is not duplicating carbohydrate counting, since COB is 0 in all 24 loop snapshots. The activation conditions are internally consistent: smb_always_enabled true is the governing switch, while smb_with_cob_enabled false and smb_after_carbs_enabled false are effectively inert while always-on is active, and the pairing of smb_with_temp_target_enabled true with smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false suppresses SMB during the raised temporary targets that this user actually sets (135 mg/dL four times). The configured SMB caps are already more conservative than AAPS defaults (15 and 20 minutes versus 30) and against a basal of 0.5 to 0.8 U/h they are small: 20 minutes at 0.6 U/h is about 0.2 U, matching the observed standardMaxBolus 0.2. These caps are nevertheless not the binding constraint, because build-specific boost logic multiplies past them: standardMaxBolus 0.2 followed by microbolusing 0.4 U on 2026-08-07, an increased SMB percentage message on 2026-08-18 with insulinReq 1.45, and a UAM high boost with SMB equal to 1.6 U on 2026-08-19 while IOB was already 4.73 U. Those boost terms are not exposed as configurable items in the supplied inventory, so tightening the SMB minute caps would scale only the base of a larger multiplier. Critically, the overnight lows cannot be attributed to SMB or UAM settings, because in that window the loop is already delivering zero temp basal with negative IOB.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is disabled while dynamic sensitivity is enabled at a 70 percent adjustment factor, with both autosens target flags false. The sensitivity_ratio field is not fixed at 1: values of 0.79, 0.88, 0.91, 0.92, 0.94 and 0.98 appear, and a ratio of 1 is treated as a neutral current adjustment rather than as evidence that adaptation is off. The operative consequence is that effective sensitivity swings from 124 mg/dL per unit when glucose is low to 27.8 mg/dL per unit when glucose is high, so post-peak corrections are delivered at roughly double the strength of the declared ISF anchor of 56. This is the single most defensible tuning lever available in the AAPS set for the observed pattern of high afternoons followed by evening and overnight lows. A material inconsistency is that effective target_bg varied between 80 and 116 mg/dL and tracked the sensitivity ratio (ratio 0.79 with target 116, ratio 0.88 with target 108, ratio 0.94 with target 104, ratio 1 with target 80 at high glucose) even though both autosens target flags are false and only five temporary targets exist, which means an adaptive-target mechanism outside the declared flags is acting and profile target edits have weak leverage. On the safety limits, max_basal of 12 U/h is not the operative ceiling, since the loop enforced maxSafeBasal 4 U/h on 2026-08-14 (adjusted required rate 5.9 reduced to 4); 12 U/h is 15 to 24 times profile basal and is a scale mismatch rather than an active risk. max_iob of 25 U is materially different: against a profile basal of 16.2 U per day it provides no effective ceiling, and observed IOB peaks of 4.73 U and 5.935 U immediately preceded the largest falls, with reason strings showing minGuardBG of -4, -59 and 28. The carbohydrate absorption settings min_5m_carbimpact 8 and meal_max_absorption_hours 7 are functionally inert in this dataset because COB is always zero, so they can neither be validated nor invalidated. One item is noted for awareness only and not as a therapy recommendation: max_allowed_bolus_units of 8 U is large relative to observed boluses of 0.05 to 2.4 U at this daily insulin scale.

analysis_steps.findings: The user declaration in aaps_profile.analysis_context exists and is dated 2026-08-21T21:08:10 with source declared_by_user, but its meal_strategies list is empty, period_exceptions is null and strategy_stable_for_period is null. There is therefore no declared prebolus minutes value, no declared immediate bolus percentage and no declared e-carb parameters in the package to reproduce, and because strategy_stable_for_period is not true no representative declared values can be adopted for the period, which caps confidence at low. Observed execution is unambiguous: there is no identifiable meal bolus anywhere. All 655 insulin entries totalling 275.95 U are typed as correction bolus, and the size distribution of 0.05 to 0.65 U with about 47 events per day matches SMB output rather than meal dosing; only three entries stand apart as plausibly manual (2.4 U on 2026-08-15 at 12:25 local, 1.1 U on 2026-08-14 at 17:30 local, 0.85 U on 2026-08-20 at 21:40 local). Effective execution is therefore zero prebolus, zero immediate bolus percentage and full reliance on UAM. The response windows show the expected reactive signature: insulin arriving after the rise (100 to 188 mg/dL at 60 minutes after 0.2 U; 110 to 161 at 120 minutes after 0.1 U), deep falls two to four hours after a high (234 to 56 in 120 minutes; 264 to 96 in 120 minutes; 172 to 47 in 240 minutes), and fall-then-spike sequences (141 to 71 at 60 minutes then 225 at 120 minutes; 206 to 102 then 53 then 158) that strongly suggest unlogged rescue carbohydrate contaminating those windows. This resolves an earlier competing hypothesis: the 09:00 to 17:00 elevation is best explained by unannounced meals plus unavoidably late UAM response rather than by a midday basal defect, so it must not drive a basal change. Carb ratio remains unexercised and unverifiable, bolus_wizard_percentage of 100 percent is irrelevant while no wizard is used, and announcing carbohydrate would not remove SMB coverage because smb_always_enabled is true.

No aggregate value is used to infer a duration, because no meal-linked evidence exists to attach it to. The absorption settings min_5m_carbimpact 8 mg/dL per 5 minutes and meal_max_absorption_hours 7 h have had no influence on any decision in this period because COB is always zero. Extended carbohydrate entry is not equivalent to a pump extended bolus and is not evaluated as one; it would announce carbohydrate arriving over time so the loop can build COB and dose dynamically. The sustained 11:00 to 17:00 plateau (means 132.3, 141.3, 135.0, 148.1, 153.0, 162.8 and 148.9 mg/dL) is the kind of prolonged rise for which extended entry is conceptually relevant, but with no carbohydrate amounts, no composition and no absorption observations in the package, asserting that e-carbs are indicated would require inventing data, so this stage is blocked.

analysis_steps.findings: A contradiction audit against aaps_profile, profile_context and decision_inventory produced four corrections and confirmations. First, the earlier idea that the 09:00 to 17:00 elevation reflects insufficient midday basal is withdrawn: with zero carbohydrate entries the elevation is explained by unannounced meals and reactive UAM, so no daytime basal increase is proposed and the 0.5 U/h segment at 16:00 is kept. Second, the earlier reading that a sensitivity_ratio of 1 indicated inactive adaptation is corrected: ratios of 0.79 to 0.98 are present and dynamic sensitivity is clearly active. Third, the assumption that declared targets govern the loop is corrected: effective target_bg ranged from 80 to 116 mg/dL and tracked the sensitivity ratio although both autosens target flags are false and only five temporary targets exist, so target edits have weak leverage and confidence in any target change is lowered to the point where no target change is proposed. Fourth, the profile is confirmed complete and authoritative under profile_context, with 17 profile items and 6 AAPS items reproduced, so nothing is reported as missing that the package supplies. Several mechanisms remain unseparated and all predict the same signature of high afternoons followed by evening and overnight lows: dynamic ISF strength at 70 percent, DIA of 10 h, the build-specific UAM boost multipliers, and the absence of carbohydrate announcement. Because they cannot be separated from this data, exactly one dosing-strength change is proposed in this cycle. The dynamic ISF adjustment factor is chosen as the primary lever because it is directly evidenced (effective sensitivity of 27.8 to 43 mg/dL per unit at high glucose against an anchor of 56), it acts precisely where the overcorrection happens, and it is reversible in a single step; the profile ISF anchor, DIA and the SMB minute caps are deliberately held so the effect can be attributed. One further change is proposed only because it changes the safe action order rather than daily dosing: reducing max_iob from 25 U, which is meaningless against 16.2 U per day of basal, to a value that still exceeds the observed 5.935 U peak but caps further accumulation. Overnight lows from 23:00 to 03:00 remain a genuinely separate candidate, but a basal reduction there is intentionally deferred, because automation is already at zero temp basal with negative IOB in that window and the same lows may simply be the tail of afternoon overcorrection, so the effect of the sensitivity change must be observed first.

strengths: CGM data quality is excellent and supports time-of-day analysis: 98.7 percent coverage, 5-minute cadence, 3995 valid entries, zero invalid and zero duplicate readings, and a largest gap of only 65 minutes.

Overall glycemic metrics are good despite a complex setup: time in range 86.0 percent, mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL and coefficient of variation 32.6 percent, which is below the commonly used 36 percent variability threshold.

The window from 04:00 to 08:00 local is very stable, with means of 99.5 to 110.5 mg/dL, at most 1.8 percent above range and only 1.3 to 4.8 percent below range, so the morning basal steps of 0.6, 0.7 and 0.8 U/h appear well matched.
The AAPS profile is complete and internally coherent: the seven basal segments total 16.2 U per day, which matches the profile name recorded in the profile switch on 2026-08-13.
SMB minute caps are already set more conservatively than AAPS defaults, at 15 and 20 minutes rather than 30, and SMB is suppressed during raised temporary targets, which are protective choices.
The user maintains good operational hygiene, with regular site changes on 2026-08-10, 08-13 and 08-17, sensor changes on 08-11 and 08-21, and documented notes for profile switches and GLP-1 doses.

recommendations.title: Primary: discuss softening the dynamic ISF adjustment factor
recommendations.description: This is the single primary proposal of this cycle. The declared ISF anchor is flat at 56 mg/dL per unit, but with dynamic sensitivity enabled at a 70 percent adjustment factor the loop operated at 42.5, 37.9 and 27.8 mg/dL per unit whenever glucose was high, that is roughly twice the declared strength exactly where the overcorrection occurs. The consequences are visible: falls of 234 to 56 mg/dL in 120 minutes, 264 to 96 mg/dL in 120 minutes and 172 to 47 mg/dL in 240 minutes, feeding the 18:00 to 19:00 window with 7.7 and 15.3 percent below range and the 23:00 to 03:00 window with 10.1 to 18.5 percent below range. Reducing the adjustment factor moves effective sensitivity back toward the 56 anchor at high glucose. The known trade-off is that it also moves the protective high value of 124 mg/dL per unit at low glucose toward the anchor, and afternoon time above range may increase in the short term; the expected net direction is still a reduction in lows, because the observed lows follow high-glucose overcorrection rather than baseline over-basal. Because dynamic ISF strength, DIA of 10 h and the build-specific UAM boost terms all predict the same pattern, only this one lever should move so its effect can be attributed.

success_markers: overall time below range moves toward 4 percent or lower
fewer level-2 values below 54 mg/dL in the 18:00 to 19:00 local window
peak insulin on board stays below about 4 U
stop_markers: time above range rises materially without any reduction in time below range
new sustained values above 250 mg/dL in the afternoon

recommendations.title: Secondary: discuss lowering the maximum IOB ceiling as a guardrail
recommendations.description: This is included because it changes the safe action order rather than daily dosing. max_iob is configured at 25 U while the profile delivers 16.2 U per day of basal, so it is not a practical ceiling. Observed insulin on board reached 4.73 U and 5.935 U immediately before the largest falls, and on 2026-08-21 at 22:09 local the loop still requested 4 U/h at an IOB of 5.935 U. A ceiling set above the observed peak but far below 25 U would leave normal dosing untouched while capping the accumulation that precedes the deepest lows. It should be introduced as a separate step from the sensitivity change so that the two effects remain distinguishable, and the value must be chosen with the care team, taking into account that it is unclear whether total_insulin_u of 275.95 U includes basal delivery.

suggested_change.rationale_bound: above the observed peak of 5.935 U, well below 25 U
suggested_change.sequence: introduce only after the dynamic ISF observation window has been evaluated

recommendations.title: Deferred: keep overnight basal unchanged and re-evaluate after the sensitivity change
recommendations.description: The 23:00 to 03:00 window carries 10.1 to 18.5 percent below range on basal 0.6 to 0.7 U/h, which on its own would suggest a small overnight basal reduction. It is deliberately deferred, for two reasons. First, in that window the loop is already delivering zero temp basal with negative insulin on board of -0.481, -0.197 and -0.03 U, which means the low is not being driven by ongoing basal delivery at that moment. Second, the same lows may be the tail of afternoon overcorrection under a 10 h DIA, in which case the primary sensitivity change would resolve them without any basal edit. Changing basal at the same time as the sensitivity factor would make both effects unattributable.

suggested_change.condition_to_revisit: time below range between 23:00 and 03:00 local remains above about 8 percent after the sensitivity change
suggested_change.candidate_direction_if_revisited: decrease 00:00 basal by about 10 percent, one segment at a time

recommendations.title: Do not change carb ratios in this cycle
recommendations.description: The five carb ratio segments have never been exercised: zero carbohydrate entries, zero grams, COB zero in every loop snapshot and no bolus wizard use. Any change would be unverifiable and could become harmful once carbohydrate announcement begins. They should be left exactly as they are until carbohydrate entry produces observable data.

suggested_change.precondition_for_future_review: at least 7 to 10 days of entered carbohydrate amounts with timestamps

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all 17 profile rows unchanged in this cycle, including the flat ISF of 56 mg/dL per unit, DIA of 10 h, all seven basal segments and all three targets, and instead make the single change on the automation side by softening the dynamic ISF adjustment factor from 70 percent. The profile ISF anchor is deliberately held because the loop is not actually dosing at 56 mg/dL per unit; it operated between 27.8 and 124 mg/dL per unit under dynamic sensitivity, so changing the anchor and the adjustment factor together would make the result unattributable.
profile_recommendation.rationale: The evidence points at the strength of high-glucose dosing, not at the shape of the profile. The best-controlled part of the day, 04:00 to 08:00 local, sits on basal 0.6 to 0.8 U/h with at most 1.8 percent above range, so the basal grid is not broadly wrong. The afternoon elevation peaking at 162.8 mg/dL at 16:00 coincides with the lowest daytime basal of 0.5 U/h, but with zero carbohydrate entries in 14 days that elevation is better explained by unannounced meals and late UAM response, so it does not support a basal increase. Targets are held because the loop demonstrably did not use them: effective target_bg ranged from 80 to 116 mg/dL and tracked the sensitivity ratio while both autosens target flags are false and only five temporary targets exist, so a target edit may not reach the loop. Carb ratios are held because they have never been exercised. DIA of 10 h is a plausible contributor to the late tail, but it predicts the same pattern as the dynamic ISF factor and the UAM boost terms and cannot be separated from them in this data, so it is reserved for a later cycle.
profile_recommendation.next_check: After roughly 10 days on the reduced dynamic ISF adjustment factor, with no other setting changed, re-examine hourly_glucose_local for 18:00 to 19:00 and 23:00 to 03:00 and check whether time below range in those hours falls below about 8 percent and whether peak insulin on board stays under about 4 U; if the 23:00 to 03:00 window is still above 8 percent below range while the evening window has improved, the 00:00 basal segment of 0.6 U/h becomes the next single candidate.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: local hours 00 to 03 show means of 90.6 to 104.7 mg/dL with time below range of 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent, which in isolation would suggest a small reduction. Uncertainty: in that window the loop already delivers zero temp basal with negative insulin on board of -0.481, -0.197 and -0.03 U, so ongoing basal delivery is not the active driver at that moment, and the lows may instead be the tail of afternoon overcorrection under a 10 h DIA. Dependencies: the primary dynamic ISF change targets the same lows, and changing both together would make neither attributable, so this segment is held for one observation cycle and becomes the next candidate if the window stays above about 8 percent below range.

Evidence: local hours 05 to 07 are the best-controlled part of the day, with means of 104.2, 99.5 and 99.5 mg/dL, at most 1.3 to 4.8 percent below range and no time above range. Uncertainty: minimal for this window; the single 42 mg/dL value at 07:19 local on 2026-08-21 precedes a sensor change the same day and may be an artefact. Dependencies: none that would justify a change; no adjustment is supported.

Evidence: local hours 06 to 09 show 99.5, 99.5, 110.5 and 132.9 mg/dL with zero to 2.5 percent below range and at most 8.9 percent above range, so there is no dawn defect and this higher morning rate appears appropriate. Uncertainty: the rise toward 09:00 could reflect either dawn effect or unannounced breakfast, and with zero carbohydrate entries these cannot be separated. Dependencies: any morning adjustment should wait until carbohydrate announcement makes meal effects visible.

Evidence: local hours 10 to 15 show means of 148.0, 132.3, 141.3, 135.0, 148.1 and 153.0 mg/dL with 7.5 to 26.3 percent above range, which superficially suggests under-basal. Uncertainty: with zero carbohydrate entries in 14 days and COB zero in every loop snapshot, this elevation is better explained by unannounced meals and late UAM response than by basal need. Dependencies: raising basal here would increase insulin exposure that continues into the 18:00 and 19:00 low window, which already carries 7.7 and 15.3 percent below range, so no increase is supported.

Evidence: 16:00 local is the highest hour of the day at 162.8 mg/dL with 32.1 percent above range and zero percent below range, and it coincides exactly with the lowest daytime basal of 0.5 U/h. Uncertainty: the coincidence is not sufficient to prove a defect, because the same afternoons are followed by the deepest lows of the period at 18:00 and 19:00, and the low rate may be functioning as a necessary guard against them; meals in this block are entirely unannounced. Dependencies: this segment should only be reconsidered after carbohydrate announcement and after the dynamic ISF change has been evaluated.

Evidence: 18:00 local shows 7.7 percent below range with a mean of 124.2 mg/dL, and the level-2 clusters of 2026-08-13 and 2026-08-14 fall in and just after this hour. Uncertainty: those clusters follow corrections given at 14:05 and 17:20 local into high glucose, so the insulin tail rather than the basal rate is the more likely driver, and DIA of 10 h amplifies that tail. Dependencies: the primary dynamic ISF change directly targets this mechanism, so basal here is held until its effect is observed.

Evidence: 19:00 local carries the highest time below range of any hour at 15.3 percent with a mean of 105.4 mg/dL, which would isolate this segment as a candidate. Uncertainty: this hour sits directly downstream of the afternoon peak and its corrections, so it is the expected landing point of an insulin tail rather than an independent basal error, and the two cannot be separated from this data. Dependencies: held so that the single dynamic ISF change remains attributable; this hour is the primary observation target for that change.

Evidence: zero carbohydrate entries, 0.0 g total, empty carb_treatment_entries and COB zero in all 24 loop snapshots, so this ratio has never been exercised. Uncertainty: complete, since no observation exists to validate or invalidate it. Dependencies: it can only be reviewed after carbohydrate entry produces observable COB and meal responses.

Evidence: no carbohydrate has been entered in the period and no bolus wizard use is visible, with bolus_wizard_percentage at 100 percent but unused. Uncertainty: complete for this segment. Dependencies: review requires 7 to 10 days of entered carbohydrate amounts with timestamps.

Evidence: the 08:00 to 10:00 local rise from 110.5 to 148.0 mg/dL suggests morning intake, but no carbohydrate amount was ever recorded for it, so no ratio can be derived. Uncertainty: complete; the rise could also reflect dawn effect. Dependencies: this is the segment most likely to become assessable first, because the morning window carries almost no hypoglycemia and is the safest place to begin announcing carbohydrate.

Evidence: this is the strongest ratio in the profile and covers the block with the highest time above range, but with zero carbohydrate entries it has never actually been applied. Uncertainty: complete. Dependencies: strengthening any ratio in this block would add insulin upstream of the 18:00 and 19:00 low window, so it must not be changed before the hypoglycemia pattern is resolved.

Evidence: no carbohydrate entries exist for the evening block, and the 0.85 U entry at 21:40 local on 2026-08-20 is typed as a correction bolus with no associated carbohydrate. Uncertainty: complete. Dependencies: review requires carbohydrate entry data for evening meals.

Evidence: the profile declares one flat segment of 56 mg/dL per unit, but dynamic sensitivity is enabled at a 70 percent adjustment factor and the loop actually operated between 124 mg/dL per unit at glucose 70 and 27.8 mg/dL per unit at glucose 246, so 56 is an anchor rather than the delivered value. Uncertainty: the therapy response windows cannot be used to derive a numeric ISF, because their insulin_u field records only the discrete bolus of 0.05 to 2.4 U while SMB and temp basal delivery continues through the window, for example 0.2 U associated with a 178 mg/dL fall in 120 minutes. Dependencies: the anchor is deliberately held so that the single change to the dynamic ISF adjustment factor can be attributed; changing both at once would make the result uninterpretable.

Evidence: a target of 90 mg/dL during a window carrying 10.1 to 18.5 percent below range would normally invite a modest increase. Uncertainty: the loop demonstrably did not use the declared targets, operating at effective target_bg values from 80 to 116 mg/dL that tracked the sensitivity ratio while both autosens target flags are false and only five temporary targets exist in the period, so a profile target edit may not reach the loop as intended. Dependencies: how effective targets are derived in this build must be clarified before any target row is changed; until then the change is unsupported.

Evidence: the daytime target of 100 mg/dL is conventional and the 08:00 hour itself is well controlled at 110.5 mg/dL with zero percent below range. Uncertainty: the same conflict applies, since observed target_bg values of 80, 84, 86, 87, 99 and 104 mg/dL appear during the day and do not match the declared 100. Dependencies: no target change is proposed in this cycle; the dynamic ISF lever acts on the same overcorrection more directly.

Evidence: 23:00 local shows a mean of 105.7 mg/dL with 10.1 percent below range on this target. Uncertainty: the declared target is not the operative one, and this hour also sits downstream of the afternoon and evening insulin tail, so the target is not established as the driver. Dependencies: held together with the other two target rows for consistency, and reconsidered only if the overnight window remains low after the dynamic ISF change.

Evidence: a DIA of 10 h with insulin_type free_peak_oref keeps insulin accounted for deep into the tail and is consistent with the observed insulin on board peaks of 4.73 and 5.935 U and with falls arriving 120 to 240 minutes after dosing, such as 172 to 47 mg/dL at 240 minutes. Uncertainty: the package does not supply a peak time for the free peak model, and DIA, the dynamic ISF factor and the build-specific UAM boost terms all predict the same late-hypoglycemia signature, so they cannot be separated from this data. Dependencies: DIA is explicitly reserved for a later cycle so that the single dynamic ISF change stays attributable; shortening DIA at the same time would confound both.

Evidence: with zero carbohydrate entries in 14 days, UAM is the only mechanism providing meal coverage, and time in range is still 86.0 percent, so disabling either switch would enlarge the 09:00 to 17:00 elevated block that already reaches 32.1 percent above range at 16:00. UAM is not duplicating carbohydrate accounting, since COB is zero in all 24 loop snapshots. Uncertainty: UAM is the pathway through which the overcorrection is expressed, but the strength comes from the sensitivity and boost logic rather than from these two switches. Dependencies: both must remain enabled while the dynamic ISF change is evaluated, otherwise the afternoon pattern would change for a different reason.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / SMB activation conditions (smb_always_enabled, smb_with_cob_enabled, smb_after_carbs_enabled, smb_with_temp_target_enabled, smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: the group is internally consistent. smb_always_enabled true is the governing switch, so smb_with_cob_enabled false and smb_after_carbs_enabled false are effectively inert at present, and the pairing of smb_with_temp_target_enabled true with smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false suppresses SMB during the raised temporary targets this user actually sets, which were 135 mg/dL on four occasions. Uncertainty: on 2026-08-18 a 180-minute temporary target of 135 was active and the day still recorded 12.8 percent below range, which indicates the driver lies upstream of activation conditions rather than in them. Dependencies: this group becomes materially relevant once carbohydrate announcement begins, because with COB present the tighter 15-minute SMB cap applies instead of the 20-minute UAM cap; no change is supported before that.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / SMB strength and frequency (smb_interval_minutes, max_smb_basal_minutes, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes)
parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: these caps are already more conservative than AAPS defaults of 30 minutes, and against basal of 0.5 to 0.8 U/h they are small, with 20 minutes at 0.6 U/h giving about 0.2 U, matching the observed standardMaxBolus of 0.2. Crucially they are not the binding constraint: build-specific boost logic delivered 0.4 U against a 0.2 U standard cap on 2026-08-07 and an SMB of 1.6 U on 2026-08-19, and those multipliers are not exposed as configurable items in this package. Uncertainty: tightening the caps would scale only the base that a larger multiplier acts on, so the benefit is unpredictable while the cost, less prandial coverage in an already elevated afternoon, is likely. Dependencies: this is a competing lever for the same hypoglycemia signature as the dynamic ISF factor, and only one lever may move per cycle, so it is held; it may be revisited if the sensitivity change proves insufficient.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits (max_basal_u_per_hour, max_iob_units)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: max_iob of 25 U is not a practical ceiling against a profile basal of 16.2 U per day, and insulin on board reached 4.73 U on 2026-08-19 and 5.935 U on 2026-08-21 at 22:09 local, at which point the loop still requested 4 U/h with an insulin requirement of 2.12 U; loop reason strings show minimum guard values of -4, -59 and 28 mg/dL, and the largest falls of 234 to 56 and 264 to 96 mg/dL in 120 minutes followed those accumulations. A candidate of 8 U sits above the observed peak of 5.935 U, so it would not interfere with normal dosing, while capping further accumulation. max_basal is left at 12 U/h because it is already superseded by the enforced maxSafeBasal of 4 U/h visible on 2026-08-14, so changing it would have no observable effect and would only add a second simultaneous variable. Uncertainty: it is unclear whether total_insulin_u of 275.95 U includes basal delivery, so the true total daily dose is unknown and the exact ceiling must be set with the care team; on 2026-08-19 an occlusion and pump error mean recorded insulin on board may not equal delivered insulin. Dependencies: this is a guardrail rather than a dosing-strength change, but it must still be introduced as a separate step after the dynamic ISF observation window so the two effects remain distinguishable.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / Autosens and Dynamic ISF (autosens_enabled, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled, autosens_raises_target, autosens_lowers_target, dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: this is the primary change of the cycle and only the adjustment factor component moves. Against a flat ISF anchor of 56 mg/dL per unit the loop operated at 42.5, 37.9 and 27.8 mg/dL per unit whenever glucose was high, roughly twice the declared strength precisely where overcorrection occurs, and the resulting falls of 234 to 56 mg/dL in 120 minutes, 264 to 96 mg/dL in 120 minutes and 172 to 47 mg/dL in 240 minutes feed the 18:00 and 19:00 window with 7.7 and 15.3 percent below range and the 23:00 to 03:00 window with 10.1 to 18.5 percent below range, against an overall 5.1 percent below range. Sensitivity ratios of 0.79, 0.88, 0.91, 0.92, 0.94 and 0.98 confirm the adaptation is active and that a ratio of 1 simply means a neutral current adjustment. The other four components are held: autosens_enabled false and dynamic_sensitivity_enabled true define which engine runs and must stay fixed while its strength is tested, and both target flags are already false. Uncertainty: reducing the factor also pulls the protective 124 mg/dL per unit value at low glucose toward the anchor, and afternoon time above range may rise in the short term; the expected net direction is fewer lows because the observed lows follow high-glucose overcorrection rather than baseline over-basal, but this is a directional expectation rather than a certainty. Dependencies: DIA of 10 h, the ISF anchor of 56 and the SMB minute caps all predict the same signature and are deliberately held so that this single change can be attributed; the observed effective target_bg range of 80 to 116 mg/dL tracks the sensitivity ratio, so this change may also shift effective targets slightly.

Evidence: both settings are functionally inert in this period, because COB is zero in every loop snapshot, carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0 and extended_carb_entries is 0, so neither has influenced any decision and neither can be validated or invalidated. Uncertainty: meal_max_absorption_hours of 7 h is slightly longer than the common 6 h, but with no carbohydrate ever entered there is no observation to support a change, and no duration is inferred from any aggregate. Dependencies: these settings become material only if carbohydrate announcement begins, at which point they should be reviewed against real absorption observations rather than adjusted now.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Begin announcing carbohydrate for one recurring meal so the loop can build carbohydrate on board and dose proactively instead of through boosted post-hoc microboluses; keep SMB and UAM enabled throughout, since smb_always_enabled is true and announcing carbohydrate therefore does not remove SMB coverage while additionally bringing the tighter 15-minute SMB cap into play instead of the 20-minute UAM cap; leave prebolus at the current effective zero minutes and the immediate bolus percentage at the current effective zero percent until at least one carb ratio has been validated against real entries, because the ratios of 13, 11.1, 13.2, 10.5 and 12.6 g/U have never been exercised and DIA is 10 h, so front-loading insulin would add risk in windows already carrying 5.1 percent time below range; and do not introduce extended carbohydrate entry yet, because extended_carb_entries is 0 and average_extended_carb_duration_min is null, so no amount, start offset or duration can be supported, and extended carbohydrate entry is in any case not the same as a pump extended bolus.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The user declaration in analysis_context exists and is dated 2026-08-21 with source declared_by_user, but its meal_strategies list is empty and strategy_stable_for_period is null, so no declared prebolus minutes, immediate bolus percentage or e-carb fields exist in the package to compare against execution, and confidence is capped accordingly. Observed telemetry is unambiguous: all 655 insulin entries totalling 275.95 U are typed as correction bolus with a size distribution of 0.05 to 0.65 U matching SMB output at about 47 events per day, and only three entries of 2.4, 1.1 and 0.85 U stand apart as plausibly manual, so effective execution is zero prebolus and zero immediate bolus percentage with full reliance on UAM. The reactive signature is visible in the response windows, with glucose rising after dosing, for example 100 to 188 mg/dL at 60 minutes after 0.2 U, and deep falls two to four hours after a high, such as 234 to 56 mg/dL and 264 to 96 mg/dL in 120 minutes, which land in the 18:00 and 19:00 low window. Several windows also show fall-then-spike sequences such as 141 to 71 at 60 minutes then 225 at 120 minutes, which suggests unlogged rescue carbohydrate contaminating the data and further lowers confidence.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Record the carbohydrate amount and the entry timestamp for the main afternoon or evening intake between 13:00 and 19:00 local for 7 to 10 consecutive days, and separately log any rescue carbohydrate taken for a low. This single observation would make carbohydrate on board visible, allow the 10.5 and 12.6 g/U ratios to be validated for the first time, and separate true insulin-tail lows from rescue-carbohydrate rebound artefacts.

implementation_steps: Step 0, before any change: review this analysis with the care team and agree which single change to make first. Confirm from the pump and phone that the profile shown here is the one actually running, since the seven basal segments total 16.2 U per day and match the profile switch note recorded on 2026-08-13.

Step 1, data hygiene, no setting change: for 7 to 10 days, record the carbohydrate amount and entry timestamp for the main afternoon or evening intake and separately log any rescue carbohydrate. This costs nothing in safety terms and is required before any carb ratio, absorption or extended carbohydrate question can be answered.

Step 2, primary change, one parameter only: with the care team, discuss reducing the dynamic ISF adjustment factor from 70 percent in a step of 5 to 10 percentage points, for example to 60 percent. Change nothing else at the same time, and specifically leave the profile ISF anchor of 56 mg/dL per unit, DIA of 10 h, all basal segments, all targets and the SMB minute caps untouched.

Step 3, observe for about 10 days: check whether overall time below range moves toward 4 percent or lower, whether level-2 values below 54 mg/dL in the 18:00 to 19:00 local window become less frequent, and whether peak insulin on board stays below about 4 U. Stop and reconsider if afternoon time above range rises materially with no reduction in lows, or if new sustained values above 250 mg/dL appear.

Step 4, second change only if step 3 was tolerated: discuss lowering max_iob from 25 U to a value above the observed peak of 5.935 U but far below 25 U, for example 8 U, and leave max_basal at 12 U/h since it is already superseded by the enforced maxSafeBasal of 4 U/h. Observe for about 7 days.

Step 5, re-evaluate the overnight window: if time below range between 23:00 and 03:00 local is still above about 8 percent after steps 2 to 4, the 00:00 basal segment of 0.6 U/h becomes the next single candidate for a small reduction of about 10 percent, one segment at a time.

Step 6, only after carbohydrate data exists: begin announcing carbohydrate for the morning meal first, since 08:00 to 10:00 local carries almost no hypoglycemia, keep SMB and UAM enabled, and do not add prebolus timing or an immediate bolus percentage until the relevant carb ratio has been observed against real entries.

Step 7, reserved for a later cycle: only once the sensitivity change has been evaluated and carbohydrate data exists, discuss DIA of 10 h and the free peak insulin model with the care team, and obtain the configured peak time, which is not included in this data package.
Throughout: change one setting at a time, allow enough observation days between changes, keep a written note of what was changed and when, and revert promptly if lows worsen.
education: Time below range is the metric that most limits how aggressively any other setting can be tuned. At 5.1 percent overall, with 8 of 14 days above 4 percent, reducing lows generally takes precedence over reducing the afternoon highs, because the same insulin that would lower those highs also lands in the low windows a few hours later.

Dynamic ISF means the sensitivity used by the loop is not the number written in the profile. Here the profile shows a flat 56 mg/dL per unit, while the loop actually worked between 124 and 27.8 mg/dL per unit depending on glucose. When judging whether corrections are too strong, the effective value matters, not the profile value.

A sensitivity ratio of 1 means the current adjustment is neutral, not that adaptation is switched off. Values of 0.79 to 0.98 also appear in this data, which shows the sensitivity calculation is active throughout.

When several settings predict the same pattern, changing them together makes the result unreadable. Dynamic ISF strength, DIA of 10 h and the SMB behaviour all predict high afternoons followed by evening lows, so moving one at a time is the only way to learn which one mattered.

Insulin on board is worth watching as a safety signal in its own right. Peaks of 4.73 and 5.935 U against a basal of about 16 U per day are large, and in this data they consistently preceded the steepest falls.

Unannounced meals push the loop into a permanently reactive mode. Without carbohydrate entry the algorithm can only react to a rise that has already started, which typically produces a high peak followed by a strong late correction, exactly the shape visible between 16:00 and 19:00 local here.

Extended carbohydrate entry and a pump extended bolus are different things. Extended carbohydrate entry tells the loop that carbohydrate will arrive over time so it can build carbohydrate on board and dose dynamically; it does not itself schedule a fixed insulin delivery.

Device and context events change how data should be read. An occlusion and pump error on 2026-08-19, GLP-1 doses on three days and a sensor change on 2026-08-21 all affect specific days, so those days should not be interpreted purely as settings effects.

A single low value immediately before a sensor change, such as the 42 mg/dL at 07:19 local on 2026-08-21, may be a sensor artefact rather than a true low, which is one reason clusters of low readings are more informative than isolated points.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only and not medical advice. TuneMyBG prepares data for review; it does not diagnose, prescribe or change any pump or AAPS setting.
Every proposed change must be independently verified with the diabetes care team before it is applied, and no change should be made automatically or in bulk.

Make only one change at a time, allow an adequate observation window, and monitor glucose closely afterwards, with particular attention to the 18:00 to 19:00 and 23:00 to 03:00 local windows where lows currently cluster.

Time below range is already above the commonly used 4 percent target, with level-2 values of 41 and 42 mg/dL recorded. Any change that could increase insulin delivery must be discussed with the care team first, and rescue carbohydrate should be kept accessible.

The suggested candidate values, such as 60 percent for the dynamic ISF adjustment factor and 8 U for max_iob, are discussion starting points derived from this data package only. The care team should set the final values, taking into account information not present here.

This analysis is based on partial telemetry: only 40 of 2315 treatments and 24 of 6214 device statuses were supplied, no carbohydrate was ever recorded, no insulin peak time is given, and it is unclear whether the 275.95 U total includes basal delivery. Conclusions drawn from those areas carry correspondingly lower confidence.
If severe or repeated low glucose occurs, or if pump delivery problems such as the occlusion recorded on 2026-08-19 recur, seek prompt clinical advice rather than adjusting settings independently.
